title: Can you give me a hand?
description: Can you help me with this task?
details:
Example: Can you give me a hand with these boxes?

Usage: Conversational; add with to explain what you need help with.

title: Could you show me how?
description: Please demonstrate how to do it.
details:
Example: I haven’t used this before. Could you show me how?

Usage: A polite request when learning a task or using equipment.

title: I’m working on it
description: I’m doing that task, but haven’t finished.
details:
Example: Have you finished the report? I’m working on it.

Usage: Useful for a brief progress update; add an expected finish time if you can.

title: I’ll get back to you
description: I’ll reply after checking or thinking about it.
details:
Example: I’ll check the dates and get back to you.

Usage: Make the promise clearer by adding when you’ll reply.

title: Can I check something?
description: I’d like to ask about a detail.
details:
Example: Can I check something? Is this due on Friday?

Usage: A polite way to introduce a question.

title: When is it due?
description: What is the deadline for this work?
details:
Example: When is the essay due?

Usage: Use due for the date or time something must be submitted.

title: I need a bit more time
description: I can’t finish within the current time available.
details:
Example: I need a bit more time to finish this.

Usage: Explain how much extra time you need when requesting an extension.

title: I’m running a bit late
description: I’m behind schedule and may arrive later than planned.
details:
Example: I’m running a bit late. I’ll be there in ten minutes.

Usage: Useful for keeping someone informed; give a realistic arrival time.

title: Shall we get started?
description: Are we ready to begin?
details:
Example: Everyone’s here. Shall we get started?

Usage: Useful at the beginning of a meeting or group task.

title: What do you think?
description: What is your opinion or feedback?
details:
Example: Here’s the first draft. What do you think?

Usage: Invite feedback; name the part you want feedback on if needed.

title: Could you send me…?
description: Please send me the thing I need.
details:
Example: Could you send me the notes?

Usage: A polite request for a file, link, document, or other item.

title: Let’s go through it
description: Let’s look at it carefully together.
details:
Example: Let’s go through the instructions first.

Usage: Useful for reviewing a document or explaining steps.

title: Just to check…
description: I want to confirm that I’ve understood correctly.
details:
Example: Just to check, are we meeting online?

Usage: A short introduction to a question about a detail.

title: I’m not sure how to…
description: I don’t know the correct way to do something.
details:
Example: I’m not sure how to upload the file.

Usage: Follow with a verb without -ing: how to use it.

title: I’ve finished…
description: I’ve completed this task or activity.
details:
Example: I’ve finished the slides.

Usage: Use a noun or -ing form: I’ve finished checking the figures.

title: I haven’t finished yet
description: The task is still incomplete.
details:
Example: I haven’t finished yet. I’ve got one section left.

Usage: Yet makes it clear you expect to finish later.

title: I’m falling behind
description: I’m making less progress than I need to.
details:
Example: I’m falling behind with my reading.

Usage: Use with or on to name the work you are struggling to keep up with.

title: I need to catch up
description: I need to do work or learning I’ve missed.
details:
Example: I need to catch up on last week’s lectures.

Usage: Use on for missed work or information; this differs from social catching up.

title: Could you check this?
description: Please look at this for mistakes or problems.
details:
Example: Could you check this before I send it?

Usage: Explain what you want checked if the task is large.

title: Let’s try a different way
description: Let’s use another approach.
details:
Example: This isn’t working. Let’s try a different way.

Usage: A practical suggestion when the current approach isn’t helping.
